summary: Verified the XmlSigningService SOAP-Header-aware append fix in /app/ebms-adapter/crypto-service. Downloaded OpenJDK 21.0.2 (aarch64) to /tmp and Apache Maven 3.9.9 to /tmp (project requires JDK 21 + Maven >=3.9; Debian's apt only had OpenJDK 17 and Maven 3.8.7 which failed the maven-enforcer-plugin rules). Authored a new focused JUnit 5 + Mockito unit test (XmlSigningServiceTest) with 5 cases covering SOAP 1.1, SOAP 1.2, literal-tag fallback, non-SOAP root fallback (regression), and an anti-regression assertion that Signature is NEVER a direct child of Envelope. Ran `mvn -pl ebms-common,crypto-service -am test -Dtest=XmlSigningServiceTest -Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false` — BUILD SUCCESS, Tests run: 5, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0 in 5.894 s. Bug fix confirmed working: after sign(), the <ds:Signature> element's parentNode is the SOAP <Header> element (both SOAP 1.1 and SOAP 1.2 namespaces), and for non-SOAP XML the Signature is still appended to doc.getDocumentElement() as before.

minor.issue: Literal-tag fallback branches (getElementsByTagName('soapenv:Header') / 'SOAP-ENV:Header') are effectively unreachable in the normal namespace-aware parse path used by parseXml() because a properly namespaced Envelope will already have matched one of the two namespace-URI lookups. They only trigger for pathological SOAP-ish XML whose Envelope carries a non-standard namespace URI while still using the literal soapenv:/SOAP-ENV: prefix (as covered by the sign_shouldAppendSignatureToLiteralSoapenvHeader_whenNoNamespace test). Not a bug, but consider a code comment clarifying intent.

action_items: None required for the reported bug — fix is verified and passes 5 targeted assertions including SOAP 1.1, SOAP 1.2, literal-prefix fallback, non-SOAP regression, and anti-regression 'never under Envelope'.
Optional: add a small javadoc note on sign() clarifying that the literal-tag fallbacks are defensive-only (namespace lookups will normally succeed first).

Optional follow-up (out of scope of this bug): consider also inserting the Signature in the WS-Security-standard location — inside a <wsse:Security> element under the SOAP Header — rather than as a direct child of <soapenv:Header>. Direct child of Header is schema-legal but WS-Security compliance typically requires a wsse:Security wrapper with mustUnderstand semantics. Confirm this matches the Digikoppeling ebMS2 profile expectations before shipping.
critical_code_review_comments: XmlSigningService.sign() implementation matches the requested contract exactly: parse → try SOAP 1.1 NS Header → SOAP 1.2 NS Header → literal soapenv:Header → literal SOAP-ENV:Header → fallback doc.getDocumentElement(); signatureParent.appendChild(signature.getElement()) is used unchanged; still uses Apache Santuario XMLSignature (not javax.xml.crypto.dsig).
The new `import org.w3c.dom.Node` is used correctly (signatureParent declared as Node so both Element root and Header can be assigned).

verify() was NOT changed and continues to locate Signature via getElementsByTagNameNS(SignatureSpecNS, 'Signature'), which correctly finds the Signature wherever it lives (Envelope OR Header) — so round-trip sign→verify inside the same service is unaffected.

Regression check on the two existing Testcontainers-based tests (CryptoServiceApplicationTests, CryptoAuditLogRepositoryIntegrationTest) was NOT executed because Docker is not available in this sandbox; but those tests exercise Spring context wiring + Postgres audit persistence and are structurally unrelated to the DOM-append change, so regression risk is low.

rca of the issue: Original bug: XmlSigningService.sign() appended the enveloped XMLSignature directly under doc.getDocumentElement(), which for SOAP envelopes is <soapenv:Envelope>. Per SOAP schema, <Envelope> only permits <Header> and <Body> as children; a foreign <ds:Signature> child causes SAAJ/Apache CXF at the receiver to reject or silently strip the signature, so the receiving orchestrator perceived the message as unsigned. Fix (verified): locate the SOAP Header via a 4-tier lookup (SOAP 1.1 NS → SOAP 1.2 NS → literal 'soapenv:Header' → literal 'SOAP-ENV:Header') and use that as the append-parent; keep doc.getDocumentElement() as the safe fallback for non-SOAP XML. Reproduction pre-fix would have shown Signature.parentNode = Envelope in the test; post-fix (validated) shows Signature.parentNode = Header (localName='Header', namespaceURI = SOAP 1.1/1.2 URI) for SOAP inputs and = documentElement for plain XML.
